name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)

ministry.name: Ministry of Finance
ministry.department: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

overview: A guaranteed pension scheme mainly targeted at workers in the unorganised sector, offering a fixed monthly pension between Rs. 1,000 and Rs. 5,000 after the age of 60 based on contributions made.
objectives: Provide old-age income security for unorganised sector workers
Encourage retirement savings among informal workers

benefits.title: Guaranteed Monthly Pension
benefits.description: Fixed pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 per month after age 60, based on contribution amount and entry age

otherCriteria: Indian citizens with a savings bank/post office account, not covered under any statutory social security scheme

Fill APY registration form with nominee details
Choose desired pension amount
Contributions auto-debited monthly/quarterly/half-yearly

faqs.question: What is the pension amount range?
faqs.answer: Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 per month depending on contribution.

name: National Pension System (NPS)

ministry.name: Ministry of Finance
ministry.department: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

overview: A voluntary, defined-contribution pension system enabling individuals to systematically save for retirement through market-linked investment options managed by regulated pension fund managers.
objectives: Provide a market-linked, portable retirement savings option
Offer flexibility in fund and investment choice

benefits.title: Market-linked Returns
benefits.description: Investment across equity, corporate bonds and government securities for potentially higher long-term returns

benefits.title: Tax Benefits
benefits.description: Additional tax deduction available under Section 80CCD

otherCriteria: Any Indian citizen, resident or non-resident, within the specified age band

applicationProcess.description: Register online via eNPS or through a Point of Presence
Complete KYC and choose pension fund manager
Make contributions to Tier-I/Tier-II account
Avail annuity/lump-sum on retirement as per NPS exit rules

faqs.question: Is NPS mandatory for private sector employees?
faqs.answer: No, it is voluntary for private sector and self-employed individuals; mandatory for most central government employees who joined after 2004.

faqs.question: What tax benefits are available?
faqs.answer: Deduction under Section 80C and additional deduction under Section 80CCD(1B).

name: Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 (EPS-95)
overview: A statutory pension scheme for employees in the organised sector, providing pension benefits on retirement, disability, or to family members on death of the member, funded through employer contributions.
objectives: Provide pension security to organised sector employees
Offer family/widow pension in case of member's death
Provide disability pension for permanently incapacitated members

benefits.title: Monthly Pension
benefits.description: Pension payable on completion of eligible service or on superannuation

benefits.title: Family Pension
benefits.description: Pension to dependents in the event of the member's death

otherCriteria: EPF members with employer contributing to the pension fund; minimum 10 years of eligible service for pension

applicationProcess.description: Employer registers employee under EPF/EPS on joining
Employer contributes a share of wages to the pension fund
On retirement/eligibility, apply through EPFO portal for pension
Monthly pension credited to bank account

faqs.question: What is the minimum service required for pension?
Who contributes to EPS?
faqs.answer: A portion of the employer's EPF contribution is diverted to the pension fund; employees do not contribute separately to EPS.

name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM)
overview: A voluntary and contributory pension scheme for unorganised sector workers, providing an assured monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60.
objectives: Provide old-age protection for unorganised sector workers
Ensure assured minimum pension after retirement age
Cover workers such as street vendors, domestic workers and construction workers

benefits.title: Assured Monthly Pension
benefits.description: Rs. 3,000 monthly pension after age 60 with matching government contribution

otherCriteria: Not a member of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (government-funded) and not an income taxpayer

applicationProcess.description: Visit nearest Common Service Centre or self-enrol on maandhan.in
Provide Aadhaar and bank account details
Pay first monthly contribution
Receive PM-SYM card and continue monthly contributions until 60

faqs.question: What is the pension amount?
faqs.answer: Assured Rs. 3,000 per month after age 60.

faqs.question: Is government contribution matched?
faqs.answer: Yes, an equal matching contribution is made by the Central Government.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)

ministry.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
ministry.department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

overview: A voluntary and contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers, providing an assured monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60.
objectives: Provide social security to small and marginal farmers in old age
Encourage voluntary retirement savings among farmers

benefits.title: Assured Monthly Pension
benefits.description: Rs. 3,000 monthly pension after age 60 with matching government contribution

otherCriteria: Small and marginal farmers with cultivable landholding up to 2 hectares, not covered under other statutory pension schemes

customQuestions.question: Are you an Indian citizen?
Are you between 18 and 40 years of age?
Are you a landholding farmer?
Do you have cultivable agricultural land in India?
Is your cultivable landholding 2 hectares or less, according to the land records of the concerned State/UT?
Is your name recorded as the eligible landholder in the applicable State/UT land records?
Do you hold institutional land?
Are you a former/present Minister, MP, MLA/MLC, Municipal Corporation Mayor, District Panchayat President or constitutional office holder?
Are you a serving/retired government employee/officer or employee of a Central/State Government department, PSU, autonomous institution or local body, other than the specified exceptions?
Have you paid income tax in the previous assessment year?
Are you a registered and practicing professional such as a doctor, engineer, lawyer, chartered accountant or architect?
Are you already enrolled in PM-SYM or the National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (PM-LVM/NPS-Traders)?
Are you already covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO?

applicationProcess.description: Visit nearest Common Service Centre for enrolment
Provide Aadhaar, land and bank details
Pay first monthly contribution as per entry age
Continue contributions until age 60 to receive pension

faqs.question: Who is eligible for PM-KMY?
faqs.answer: Small and marginal farmers aged 18-40 with landholding up to 2 hectares.

faqs.question: Can PM-KISAN beneficiaries contribute via their PM-KISAN benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, eligible farmers can opt to have the contribution deducted directly from their PM-KISAN benefit.
